learningObjectives: Explain why every exported Message becomes two Modules and two TestSteps (Request + Response).
Choose the correct export option among API Test Case, OSV Scenario, WSE Test Case, and XML/JSON Test Case.
Select multiple Messages in the API Scan using Ctrl+click and export them together.
Locate the exported Component Folder in Tosca Commander and rename it appropriately.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: One Message In, Two Modules and Two TestSteps Out

elements.description: Every Message exported from the API Scan becomes TWO Modules and TWO TestSteps: one pair for the Request, one pair for the Response. This lets Tosca both steer the SUT (send the request) and set/verify dynamic parameters (read the response). The Modules hold the technical information needed to steer the system under test.

elements.text: This Request+Response pairing is the single biggest structural difference between an API TestCase and a UI TestCase — every function-performing Message needs both halves present to be complete.

bulletPoints: 1 exported Message = 2 Modules + 2 TestSteps (Request pair + Response pair).
A Request without its matching Response (or vice versa) is an incomplete TestCase.

rows: The standard option used throughout this course for REST and SOAP messages.
Covered separately in the dedicated OSV (Orchestrated Service Virtualization) course.
Legacy option — WSE Scenarios will no longer be supported in future versions of the API Scan and Tosca, so it is not covered in this course.
Used specifically for XML/JSON file scans — covered later in the XML TestCases section of this course.

elements.title: Exporting selected Messages
items: In Tosca Commander, select or create the destination Component Folder. If none is selected, the export lands in the root element, inside an auto-created folder.
In the API Scan, select the Messages to export. Shift+click does NOT work here — hold Ctrl and click each Message individually to multi-select.
Click the "API Test Case" button in the ribbon to export.
By default the new Component Folder is named "ApiScan_Import" — rename it to something identifiable.

bulletPoints: Use Ctrl+click (not Shift+click) to multi-select Messages before exporting.
Rename the default "ApiScan_Import" folder immediately so your project stays organized.
WSE is being phased out; OSV and XML/JSON exports serve different, specific purposes.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting one Module per exported Message
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume exporting a single Message produces a single Module and a single TestStep.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Every exported Message produces TWO Modules and TWO TestSteps — one Request pair and one Response pair — because Tosca needs both halves to steer the SUT and verify/set dynamic parameters.

examPitfalls.title: Using Shift+click to multi-select Messages
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates try Shift+click to select a range of Messages in the API Scan, as they might in Windows Explorer.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Shift+click does not work in the API Scan for multi-selection. Hold Ctrl and click each Message individually instead.

examPitfalls.title: Choosing WSE Test Case for new work
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates pick the WSE Test Case export option out of habit or because it appears first in a list.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: WSE Scenarios will no longer be supported in future versions of the API Scan and Tosca. Use API Test Case (REST/SOAP), OSV Scenario, or XML/JSON Test Case depending on the use case.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How many Modules and TestSteps does Tosca create when a single Message is exported from the API Scan as an API Test Case?

options.text: Two Modules and two TestSteps — one Request pair, one Response pair.
It depends entirely on the HTTP Method used.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what Tosca needs to both send a request and check what comes back.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Every exported Message becomes two Modules and two TestSteps: one pair for the Request, one pair for the Response — letting Tosca both steer the SUT and set/verify dynamic parameters.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does a tester select multiple Messages in the API Scan before exporting them together?

options.text: Hold Shift and click the first and last Message.
Hold Ctrl and click each Message individually.
Messages can only be exported one at a time.

practiceQuiz.hint: Shift+click, which works in many file explorers, does NOT work here.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Shift+click range-selection shortcut does not work in the API Scan. Ctrl+click is used to select multiple Messages or Operations individually before exporting.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which export option will Tricentis Tosca and the API Scan stop supporting in future versions?
practiceQuiz.hint: This is explicitly called out as being phased out.
practiceQuiz.rationale: WSE Scenarios will no longer be supported in future versions of the API Scan and Tosca, which is why they are not covered in this course. API Test Case, OSV Scenario, and XML/JSON Test Case remain supported.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the default name of the Component Folder created in Tosca Commander when you export Messages without first selecting a destination folder?
practiceQuiz.hint: It's descriptive of what just happened — an import from the API Scan.
practiceQuiz.rationale: If no Component Folder is selected before exporting, Tosca creates one by default named "ApiScan_Import", which should be renamed to something more identifiable.
